objections.claim: Advertising SARIF for `analyze` requires two §7.1-parked identity recipes — RunId and the finding fingerprint — so the slice's sharpest feature contradicts its own rationale sentence 'touching NOTHING the V1 chain blocks'. D-002 defers baseline/ratchet BECAUSE fingerprints are parked, then silently ships SARIF, which needs the same parked recipe plus RunId.
objections.evidence: DR-122's required acceptance evidence (file 08 L246) reads 'parity/loss goldens preserving canonical Run/Finding IDs, Coverage, verdict, truncation, and artifact references', and its blueprint impact is 'Hard blocker for any first-slice command or reporting component that advertises SARIF'. DR-G17 (L290) requires 'serialized typed/native and namespaced fields for Run/Finding IDs, Coverage, verdict…'. Freeze §7.1 parks 'RunId derivation' ('No exact RunId derivation recipe is binding yet') and 'Finding fingerprint recipe' with the load-bearing note 'No artifact defines a Finding schema' (freeze L1696, L1699). D-002 includes DR-122 in the condition-2 affected set and G17 (analyze) in the required-gate set, so under D-001's condition 2 those rows must reach SATISFIED — which their own acceptance evidence makes impossible without the parked recipes. D-002's baseline deferral names this exact dependency for fingerprints ('needs stable finding fingerprints, which are a §7.1 parked recipe (DR-006)') and names nothing for SARIF. The dispatch criterion applies: if the slice cannot ship the feature without a parked recipe, D-002 must drop it or name the dependency — silence is the blocker.
objections.proposedFix: Either (a) move SARIF advertisement out of slice 1 with the same explicit-deferral honesty baseline/ratchet received, or (b) keep it and record in D-002 that SARIF-for-analyze is conditional on DR-006 closing RunId + finding fingerprint (+ Coverage fields) by route A — and in either case strike or qualify the rationale sentence 'touching NOTHING the V1 chain blocks'.

objections.claim: Even without SARIF, the slice as drafted exercises at least four §7.1-parked or freeze-named identity gaps: the Finding schema, cache/regeneration keys, subjectScopeCommitment, and typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot. The 'exercises every UNBLOCKED architectural surface … while touching NOTHING the V1 chain blocks' rationale is false on the freeze's own bytes.
objections.evidence: (a) Finding schema: the slice promises 'stable human and machine (JSON) output for every command' while freeze §7.1's fingerprint row states 'No artifact defines a Finding schema' — stable machine output of findings cannot be designed as settled. (b) Cache/regeneration keys: the slice's state model is 'rebuildable cache/index' (DR-124), and §7.1 parks 'cache and regeneration key recipes' with 'Coverage keys are compared for exact equality across cache lookup and provider dispatch; a divergent key silently changes cache behavior' (freeze L1701) — the named state class is keyed by a parked identity. (c) subjectScopeCommitment: parked at freeze L1703, 'required on every Coverage key', computation/verification 'still owned by the retention/evidence surface and … REOPENED'; the slice's one language role rides the TypeScript provider protocol whose contract (file 02, 'TypeScript provider') carries commitments and Coverage. (d) typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot: file 08's DR-006 park-coverage note records it as a 'PlanId-affecting digest with no producing rule' — TypeScript is the slice's only role. (e) DR-124's own acceptance evidence includes 'Plan/Run … rules', and RunId/PlanId inputs are the parked surfaces above. Condition 1 will force a DR-006 outcome regardless; but if it closes by route-B disposition (recipes stay unsettled), the slice's analyze/cache/state design is blocked, and if by route A, the slice DOES wait on an evidence-identity successor — contradicting 'without waiting on the evidence/custody successors' either way.
objections.proposedFix: Replace the absolute rationale with a named dependency set: slice-1 blueprint depends on DR-006 closing, at minimum, the Finding schema/fingerprint, cache/regeneration keys, subjectScopeCommitment, and the TypeScript PlanId-affecting digests — by route A, or by a scoped route-B disposition that explicitly licenses non-authoritative interim keys/schemas with named consequences (no stability promise, no baseline, no SARIF canonical IDs). State which route the slice presumes.

objections.claim: The condition-2 half-row inclusions of DR-106, DR-109, and DR-113 are unlawful splits: condition 2 quantifies over rows with exactly two outcomes (SATISFIED, or deferred with disposition), the three rows' own acceptance evidence begins with applied DR-002–008 successors, and D-001 itself classified all three as inherit-blocked. Including their 'halves' in the affected set makes readiness wait on the very successors the rationale claims not to wait for — or requires register surgery no one has decided.
objections.evidence: File 08: DR-106 acceptance evidence 'Applied DR-002–008; clean-machine no-network tests; durable retention and typed storage-failure results' (L230); DR-109 'Applied evidence successor; one-writer commit, custody, recovery…' (L233); DR-113 'DR-002–008 successors; exact typed results/exits…' (L237). None of the three rows contains a severable non-authoritative half in its own text. DR-113's purge half is expressly blocked elsewhere: DR-007's blueprint impact reads 'V2 cannot define replay/purge/degradation typed result or exit' (L40), so a slice-1 'purge half' of DR-113 designs a typed result DR-007 forbids. D-001 §3 condition-2 classification reads 'Inherit-blocked: DR-106, DR-109, DR-113, DR-124 (its evidence class)' — D-002 contradicts its own adopted predecessor without saying so. D-001 also holds 'Register-content changes are DECISIONS, not hygiene' and (turn-2 NOTE-1) that the checklist text and the register must never disagree; evaluating condition 2 over invented half-rows disagrees with both.
objections.proposedFix: Remove DR-106/109/113 from the affected set and defer each ENTIRELY with an explicit disposition stating: the slice has no authoritative closure/storage/replay/evidence-purge surface; its local needs route through DR-124 (cache/metadata classes), DR-114 + DR-G12 (doctor/local purge honesty), DR-107 + DR-G18 (locks/generations), DR-101 + DR-G01..G05 (install closure). Alternatively, commission the row splits as reviewed register amendments (the C4a mechanism D-001 already established) BEFORE condition 2 is evaluated.

objections.claim: The DR-110 deferral is lawful in principle but unsupported as drafted: the required-gate set includes DR-G08 unscoped, whose claim covers 'core/component/repair trust survives expiry, revocation, quorum loss, rollback' — repair/rollback being DR-110's deferred subject — and file 02's proposed default core inventory includes 'updates', while DR-107/DR-G18 (in-slice) carry generation rollback. The deferral disposition must show nothing in-slice depends on DR-110; right now three in-slice surfaces textually overlap it.
objections.evidence: Register DR-110 impact column is an unqualified 'Hard blocker' (L234), but condition 2's own text licenses deferral of any DR-101..127 row with an explicit disposition — the impact column states what stays blocked while the row is open, not that deferral is forbidden; so the prompt-level question 'is DR-110 non-deferrable for ANY slice' resolves NO. What remains is coherence: DR-G08's claim text (L281) includes repair and rollback; file 02 'Proposed small signed distribution core' lists 'updates' in the default install; D-002 includes G08 unscoped in the required set while stating 'install is fresh signed download in slice 1'.
objections.proposedFix: Scope G08 in the gate set the way G09 is scoped — e.g. 'G08 (scoped: install/index trust, expiry, revocation, quorum loss; repair-media and self-update rollback deferred with DR-110)' — and have the DR-110 deferral disposition draw the boundary between DR-107/G18 generation rollback (in-slice) and DR-110 self-update/repair rollback (deferred), plus note that the file 02 core inventory's 'updates' entry is not exercised in slice 1.

objections.claim: D-002 is silent on which install shape slice 1 assumes, and the silence hides a dependency on hard-blocked DR-010/DR-117: a small signed core with TypeScript as a separately-lifecycled component is not the V1 G3 substrate ('full-default Rust host/core plus bundled TypeScript and pinned Rust sidecar/offline assets'), and file 10's MVP scope row for the small-core direction says 'product successor remains required' (DR-117, whose item 7 is 'replacement of the full-default G3 physical substrate').
objections.evidence: File 02 'Current V1 product boundary and required successors' lists G3 and the seven DR-117 disposition items; file 10 MVP row 4 links DR-101/106/115/117 with 'product successor remains required'; DR-010 is HARD-BLOCKED (file 08 L43). D-002's DR-117 entry hedges ('to the extent first-party component claims touch P-1/P-2/G3 — proceeds on the DR-010 track regardless') without saying whether slice 1's default distribution is a G3-compatible full bundle or presumes the small-core split — the presumption would quietly relitigate a recorded bound, which D-002's own preamble forbids.
objections.proposedFix: State the assumption: either slice 1's default install is a single signed selection containing core + the TypeScript component (G3-shape-compatible; the small-core split remains conditional on the DR-010/117 successor), or the slice presumes the split and D-002 records that as an explicit named dependency on the DR-010 track's outcome.

objections.claim: User-intent objection (dispatch axis 6): unconditionally excluding baseline/ratchet cedes the prototype's core CI capability — gating net-new findings — which is the most plausible adoption driver a product owner wants in a first slice. Since condition 1 forces a DR-006 outcome anyway, the honest decision shape is conditional, not exclusion.
objections.evidence: prototype-evidence-reference.md rows 'Baseline/ratchet': 'Corpus records existing findings; comparison gates net-new findings using stable fingerprints' — a first-class prototype capability. D-002's stated blocker (fingerprints §7.1-parked) evaporates if DR-006 closes by route A with a fingerprint recipe, which is the same closure ADV-D002-01/02 show the slice needs for SARIF and stable machine findings anyway. Excluding baseline/ratchet buys no additional decoupling once those dependencies are named honestly.
objections.proposedFix: Adopt the conditional form — baseline/ratchet is IN slice 1 if and only if DR-006 closes the finding-fingerprint recipe by route A (and OUT under a route-B disposition) — or record the disagreement for the user with the trade named: conditional inclusion couples slice-1 scope to the evidence-identity lineage head (v11, under review) and adds the comparison-gate design; exclusion ships analyze sooner but without the workflow the prototype demonstrates as the product's value.

objections.claim: DR-114's acceptance evidence ('…stable schema, D9 mapping, redaction corpus') and DR-G21's required evidence ('Coverage/D9/UI/exit goldens') depend on D9 semantics DR-007 records as gapped — 'observation→faultCause' is one of DR-007's three checker-derived gaps and is exactly the component-fault mapping path G21 exercises. D-002 puts DR-114 in the affected set and G21 in the required set without naming the dependency.
objections.evidence: File 08 DR-007 (L40): 'D9 successor for observation→faultCause, optional presence, success/policy/interrupted branch', status HARD-BLOCKED. DR-114 (L238) acceptance includes 'D9 mapping'. DR-G21 (L294) evidence includes 'Coverage/D9/UI/exit goldens'; file 02 'Independent failure containment' maps component failure 'through host Coverage/D9 rules'. Under route B for condition 1, those goldens cannot be completed; under route A the slice waits on the DR-007 successor.
objections.proposedFix: Name the dependency in D-002: DR-114's D9-mapping evidence and G21's D9 goldens are producible only after the DR-007 successor (or a scoped disposition freezing the current D9 v1.14 branch semantics for slice-1 non-authoritative use), mirroring the honesty already applied to baseline/ratchet.

objections.claim: DR-G10's membership in the condition-4 required set is left ambiguous ('DR-G10 per its selector refresh'), yet the TypeScript provider protocol major 1 is the slice's execution substrate — its conformance gate cannot be anything but required for slice 1.
objections.evidence: The slice's only language role rides the TS provider (file 02 'TypeScript provider', major 1, conformance goldens). File 08 DR-G10 (L283) is 'HARD-BLOCKED pending selector refresh'. D-001 condition 4 already prescribes 'DR-G10's selector refresh + a named V2 runner over pinned goldens'. D-002's phrasing neither includes G10 in the enumerated required list nor defers it, so the decided set has an undecided member.
objections.proposedFix: Move DR-G10 into the enumerated required set: 'G10 (TS major 1) — required; harness is the named V2 runner over pinned V1 goldens, after the selector refresh.'

objections.claim: Listing DR-G06/G11 inside the condition-4 required-gate sentence ('named now, executable only after the condition-1 chain') conflates the slice's required set with the product's eventual set: both gates guard AUTHORITATIVE closure/storage, which the slice excludes, so for slice 1 they are not required gates at all.
objections.evidence: DR-G06 claim: 'Supported authoritative product installs/runs with no network and mandatory storage'; DR-G11: 'Authoritative closure cannot succeed without verified durable storage' (file 08 L279, L284) — both BLOCKED by DR-002–008. The slice states 'Authoritative sealed closure, replay, and evidence custody are OUT of slice 1'.
objections.proposedFix: Label them explicitly: 'G06/G11: NOT slice-1-required (no authoritative surface in slice); pre-named now for hygiene, required by the first slice that includes an authoritative closure.'

objections.claim: The defensible scopings — DR-105 (permissions actually exercised), DR-124/DR-G19 (touched classes), DR-G09 (scoped) — are lawful under their rows' own text (a truth-table matrix is naturally scoped by what is requested; G19's threshold literally reads 'all stateful first-slice roles'), but each must land as the explicit 'product/architecture scope disposition' condition 2 names, not remain D-002 prose.
objections.evidence: Condition 2 (file 08 L307-308): 'deferred items have explicit product/architecture scope dispositions.' D-002's parentheticals are currently the only record of these scopes.
objections.proposedFix: Add to D-002's deferral paragraph that each scoped inclusion is itself recorded as a scope disposition with its own artifact/commit, so no scope exists only inside this register entry.

objections.claim: The overturn claim ('one-line supersession + git revert of the C2 commit') is accurate only until dependent commits land; after deferral dispositions, gate namings, and DR-118 corpus work are built on the slice, reverting C2 alone does not restore the pre-decision state, and the overturn is no longer cheaper than the decision.
objections.evidence: D-001 §5's own commit plan sequences per-disposition and per-gate commits after C2; each cites the slice.
objections.proposedFix: Add one sentence to the overturn procedure: after dependent dispositions land, overturn is a successor slice decision that must also disposition or supersede the dependents; the one-revert path is available only before them.
